definition.raw:
Let $\alpha(x)$ be a measurable function taking values in  $ [\alpha_1,\alpha_2]$ for  $0<\alpha_1\leqslant \alpha_2<2$, and
$\kappa(x,z)$ be a positive measurable function that is symmetric in $z$ and bounded
between two positive constants.
definition.clean: Let alpha(x) be a measurable function taking values in [alpha_1,alpha_2] for 0<alpha_1leqslant alpha_2<2, and kappa(x,z) be a positive measurable function that is symmetric in z and bounded between two positive constants.

Let LL be a non-local operator with variable order given by LL f(x)=int_mathds R^dbig(f(x+z)-f(x)-langlenabla f(x), zrangle mathds 1_\|z|leqslant 1\big) frackappa(x,z)|z|^d+alpha(x)\,dz, f in C_c^2(mathds R^d), where alpha:mathds R^d rightarrow (0,2) is a measurable function such that & 0<alpha_1leqslant alpha(x) leqslant alpha_2<2 hboxfor x in mathds R^d,\\ & |alpha(x)-alpha(y)|leqslant c_1(|x-y|^beta_1wedge 1) hboxfor x,yin mathds R^d, for some constants c_1in(0,infty) and beta_1in(0,1], and kappa:mathds R^dtimes mathds R^d rightarrow (0,infty) is a measurable function satisfying & kappa(x,z)=kappa(x,-z) hboxfor x,z in mathds R^d,\\ & 0<kappa_1leqslant kappa(x,z)leqslant kappa_2<infty hboxfor x,zin mathds R^d,\\ & |kappa(x,z)-kappa(y,z)|leqslant c_2(|x-y|^beta_2wedge 1) hboxfor x,y,zin mathds R^d, for some constants c_2in(0,infty) and beta_2 in (0,1].
define B(x_0, r):=\xin mathds R^d: |x-x_0|< r_0\.
define LL^y f(x):=int_mathds R^dbig(f(x+z)-f(x)-langlenabla f(x), z ranglemathds 1_\|z|leqslant 1\big)frackappa(y,z)|z|^d+alpha(y)\,dz.
we define for f:mathds R^drightarrow mathds R, delta_f(x;z):=f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x), \ x,zin mathds R^d.
define overlinealpha(y;s):=sup\alpha(z): |z-y|leqslant s\ and underlinealpha(y;s):=inf\alpha(z): |z-y|leqslant s\.
define q_n(t,x,y) inductively by q_n(t,x,y):=int_0^tint_mathds R^dq_0(t-s,x,z)q_n-1(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds,\ ngeqslant1,\ tin(0,1].
define sigma_D:=inf\t geqslant 0: X_t in D\, tau_D:=inf\t geqslant 0: X_t notin D\.

proof.raw:
Without loss of generality, throughout the proof we will assume that $\beta_0< \alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$; otherwise, we will replace $\beta_0$ by $\beta_0^*.$


(i) According to \eqref{l2-1-2}, if $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then
$$|q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y),\quad t\in(0,1] \textrm{ and } x,y \in \mathds R^d.$$
Therefore, by Corollary \ref{l3-3},
\begin{align*}|q_1(t,x,y)|\preceq&\int_0^t\int \rho_{-\gamma}^{z,\beta_0}(t-s,x-z) \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\
\preceq& \mathscr{B}\big(({\wh\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, ({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)
\big(\rho_{2(({\wh
\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0}\big)(t,x-y),\end{align*}
where $\wh \beta_0:=\beta_0 \wedge (\alpha_2/2)$.


Suppose now that
$$|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant \omega_n\Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),\quad n\geqslant0,$$
where the constant $\omega_n$ is to be determined later.
Hence, according to Corollary \ref{l3-3} again,
\begin{align*}|q_{n+1}(t,x,y)|\leqslant& C\int_0^t\int \rho_{-\gamma}^{z,\beta_0}(t-s,x-z) \omega_n \Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\wh\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\
\leqslant&C \omega_n \mathscr{B}(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n+1)(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)) \Big(\rho_{(n+2)(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y)\\
=&: \omega_{n+1}\Big(\rho_{(n+2)(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y), \end{align*} where $$ \omega_{n+1}= C \mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n+1)(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\omega_n ,$$
and $C$ is a constant independent of $t,n,x$ and $y$.
Note that $\omega_0\leqslant C$ and $\mathscr{B}(\gamma, \beta)=\frac{\Gamma(\gamma)\Gamma(\beta)}{\Gamma(\gamma+\beta)}$, where $\Gamma$ is the standard Gamma function. By iteration procedure we have
\begin{align*}\omega_n\leqslant &C^{n+1}\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, n(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\\
&\times\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n-1)(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\cdots\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, ({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)\\
=&\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}.\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{equation}\label{p3-1-6a}\begin{split}
|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant &\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)} \Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}
+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),\end{split}
\end{equation}
and so combing all estimates together
$$\sum_{n=0}^\infty |q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant \left(\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\wh\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}\right)\Big(\rho_{2(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),$$ which means that $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=0}^\infty q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent, and
$$|q(t,x,y)|\leqslant C_1  \Big(\rho_{2(({\wh\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y).$$
Thus, \eqref{p3-1-1} is proved by using the fact that $\beta_0\leqslant 2\wh \beta_0$ and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly. From \eqref{eq3-1}
and the fact $q(t,x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$, it is easy to see that $q(t,x,y)$ solves the equation \eqref{eq2-2}.

(ii) Suppose that there are some $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z\in B(y_0,r_0)$.
According to \eqref{l2-1-33a}, it is easy to verify that for every $z \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation}\label{p3-1-7a}
\begin{split}
|q_0(s,z,y_0)|&\preceq \big(|z-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot
\begin{cases}
\frac{1}{(s^{{1/\alpha(y_0)}}+|z-y_0|)^{d+\alpha(y_0)}},& |z-y_0|\leqslant r_0,\\
\frac{1}{|z-y_0|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|z-y_0|> r_0
\end{cases}\\
&\preceq \rho^{y_0,\beta_0}_0(s,z-y_0).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
This along with the fact that $|q_0(t-s,x,z)|\preceq \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,x-z)$ for every $x,z\in \mathds R^d$ yields that for all $x\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
|q_1(t,x,y_0)|&\preceq \int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,x-z)\rho^{y_0,\beta_0}_0(s,z-y_0)\,dz\,ds\\
&\leqslant C\mathscr{B}\big(({\wh\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma,({ \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)
\big(\rho^{y_0,0}_{({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})+(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}+\rho^{y_0,\beta_0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big)(t,x-y_0).
\end{align*}
Following the same arguments in part (i), we find that for every $n \geqslant 0$,
\begin{align*} |q_n(t,x,y_0)|
&\leqslant \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}
\Big(\rho_{({\wh \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})+n(({\wh\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y_0,0}+\rho_{n(({ \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y_0,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y_0),\end{align*}
which implies $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent and gives us \eqref{p3-1-2b} immediately.

(iii) It suffices to prove \eqref{p3-1-1a} for the case that $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$  holds with some $R_1>0$, since the case
that $|x-x'|>1$ follows from \eqref{p3-1-1} immediately.
For any (fixed) $ \varepsilon>0$ small enough, let $\tilde \rho^{y,\beta}_{\gamma}$ be defined by \eqref{p3-1-7}.  By \eqref{p3-1-1a-1}, we have
\begin{equation}\label{p3-1-8a}
\begin{split}
&|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\times \bigg[\left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\right)(t,x-y)  + \left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\bigg],
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where $\tilde \theta:=\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}$. Since $\beta_0^*=\beta_0<\alpha(x)$, by  \eqref{e1-3} we can find a constant
$R_1>0$ small enough such that $\beta_0< \alpha(x)\wedge\alpha(x')$ for any $x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$.
Then, according to \eqref{eq2-2}, it holds that
\begin{align*}
&|q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)|\\
&\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
|q_0(t-s,x,z)-q_0(t-s,x',z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\\
&\quad\times\bigg\{ \Big[\big(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\big)(t,x-y)
+ \left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\Big]\\
&\quad \quad+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \Big[\big(\tilde \rho^{z,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\big)(t-s,x-z)\\
&\qquad\qquad\quad\qquad+ \big(\tilde \rho^{z,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}
\big)(t-s,x'-z)\Big]
\Big[\big(
\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,z-y)\Big]\,dz\,ds \bigg\}\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\cdot\Big[\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-2\gamma
+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x-y)
+ \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-2\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big].
\end{align*}
Here the second inequality follows from \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{p3-1-8a}, thanks to the fact that
$\beta_0< \alpha(x)\wedge \alpha(x')$, and the last inequality is due to Remark \ref{r3-3}(2) (which indicates that the convolution inequality \eqref{l3-3-0} holds for $\tilde \rho$) and the fact that $\gamma<\theta$.



(iv) Now we are going to prove the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$.
Due to the assumption $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$, we can choose $\gamma>0$ small enough such that
$\gamma+({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1=:\gamma_2 <{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$. Using \eqref{l2-1-1} and following the same arguments in part (i) with $\gamma_2 $ instead of $\gamma$, we can obtain that for
every $n\geqslant 1$ and $(t,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation}\label{p3-1-9a}
\begin{split}
|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant &\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2  )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 )\big)} \bigg(\rho_{(n+1)(({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 )}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma_2 +n({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}
-\gamma_2 )}^{y,\beta_0} \bigg)(t,x-y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Using this and \eqref{l2-1-1}, we find immediately that $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)|<\infty$ and so
\eqref{p3-1-2} is true.

Note that, according to Proposition \ref{p3-1-1a-p}(2), in this case \eqref{p3-1-8a} holds with
$\gamma_2$ in place of  $\gamma $. (Note that here $\beta_0$ is not replaced by $\beta_0^{**}$.) This along with \eqref{p3-1-2} and the same argument in (iii) gives us \eqref{p3-1-2a}.


(v) Suppose that the assumptions in part (2) of the Proposition hold, and that there are some $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then, using \eqref{l2-1-33} and repeating the arguments in part (ii) above,
we can prove \eqref{p3-1-2c}.

Without loss of generality, throughout the proof we still assume that $\beta_0< \alpha_2/2$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$.

We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
As in the proof of Proposition \ref{p3-1}(1), we know that
$q(t,x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$
is absolutely convergent. In particular, \begin{equation}\label{p3-1-9}
|q(t,x,y)|\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)|+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)|.
\end{equation}
According to \eqref{p3-1-6a}, we have
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)|
& \leqslant
 \left(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}
 \right)\Big(\rho_{3(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y) \preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where in the last inequality we choose $\gamma>0$ small enough such that
$\gamma<{\beta_0}/({2\alpha_2})$.
Combining this estimate with \eqref{p2-1-1} and  \eqref{p3-1-9},  we obtain \eqref{p3-1-2e} immediately.

If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$, then one can use \eqref{p2-1-1a} and follow
the same procedure above to prove \eqref{p3-1-2f}.

Without loss of generality, throughout this proof we will assume that $2\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$; otherwise, we will replace $\beta_0$ by $\beta_0^{**}\in (0,\beta_0]\cap (0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ For simplicity, we only verify the case that $c_0=1$.

(i) We first consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
Note that $$p^z(t,x-z)\preceq \rho_1^{z,0}(t,x-z),\quad t\in (0,1],x,z\in \mathds R^d.$$ This, along with
\eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, yields that for every $(t,x,y)\in
(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$ and {any constant
$0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2},$}
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d} p^z(t-s,x-
z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\preceq
\big(\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+
\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big).
\end{equation*}
Therefore, $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and
\begin{equation}\label{p3-2-3}
p(t,x,y)\preceq \Big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+
\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\Big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq
\big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big).
\end{equation}

When $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha_2}}$,
$$\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-\gamma}|x-y|^{\beta_0}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)
\preceq t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big).$$
Hence, due to $\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we get
\begin{equation}\label{p3-2-3a}
\begin{split}
p(t,x,y)\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(y)}}\preceq
t^{-{d}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where the third inequality follows from \eqref{l3-2-8}.

Next, we will verify the other two cases in the upper bound \eqref{p3-2-1}. Observe that
for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ such that
$|x-y|\leqslant 1$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
 \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}
&=
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{({1/\alpha(y)})-({1/\alpha(x)})}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}
 \preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&\preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}})^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&=t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|(d+\alpha(y))}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}}\\
&\preceq t^{-{(d+\alpha_2)|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot
t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1}}\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}} \preceq
\frac{t^{-C_1R_0^{\beta_0}}}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality we used
$t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant 1$, and the third inequality follows from the fact that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\preceq t^{-{|\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)|}/{\alpha(x)}}.
\end{align*}
Thus, choosing $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\gamma)$ small enough  such that
$C_1R_0^{\beta_0}<\gamma$ and using the definition of $\rho^{x,0}_0$, we can
get that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with
$|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{equation}\label{l4-1-5}
\rho^{y,0}_0(t,z)\preceq t^{-\gamma}\rho^{x,0}_0(t,z).
\end{equation}
By the definition of \eqref{e3-0}, we know immediately that \eqref{l4-1-5} still holds for
every $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|> 1$. This is, \eqref{l4-1-5} holds for all $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$.

Hence, combining \eqref{p3-2-3}, \eqref{p3-2-3a} with \eqref{l4-1-5} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we find that
\begin{align*}
p(t,x,y)&\preceq
 \big(\rho^{y,0}_{1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}
\big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq \begin{cases}t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, & |y-x|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\
\frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},& t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |y-x|\leqslant R_0,\\
\frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x|> R_0.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}

(ii) If there are some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such
that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then for
every $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$ and $z \in
B(y,{r_0}/{2})$,
$
\alpha(z)=\alpha(y)=\alpha(x_0).
$
Hence, by \eqref{p3-1-2b}, we have
\begin{equation*}
|q(t,x,y)|\preceq
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_0\Big)(t,x-y)\quad\textrm{ for all }
x\in \mathds R^d\textrm{ and }y \in B\big(x_0,{r_0}/{2}\big).
\end{equation*}
Based on the inequality above, the computation in part (i) is valid
with $\gamma=0$ for $x=x_0$ and $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$, which
proves \eqref{p3-2-2} for the case that $y \in
B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$. The upper bound for the case
$|y-x_0|>{r_0}/{2}$ is just the same as that of \eqref{p3-2-1}.


(iii) If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and
${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, then, according to
\eqref{p3-1-2}, we know that the computation in part (i) holds with
$\gamma$ replaced by $\tilde\gamma$. Thus, following the argument in part
(i), we can obtain \eqref{p3-2-1a}. Similarly as in (ii),
\eqref{p3-2-2a} could be verified by using \eqref{p3-1-2c}.

proof.raw:
We write  $ \LL^y=\LL_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}^y+\LL_{\wh \kappa}^y$ with
\begin{align*}
\LL_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}^y f(x)&=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\delta_{f}(x;z)\frac{\kappa_1}{2}\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\,dz,\quad f\in C_c^2(\mathds R^d),\\
\LL_{\wh \kappa}^y f(x)&=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\delta_{f}(x;z)\frac{\wh \kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\,dz,\quad f\in C_c^2(\mathds R^d),
\end{align*}
where $\kappa_1>0$ is the constant in \eqref{e1-2}, $\wh \kappa(y,z):=\kappa(y,z)-\kappa_1/2$ and
$$\delta_f(x;z)=f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x).$$ Then, we have
\begin{equation}\label{l4-4-2}
p^y(t,x)=\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)p^y_{\wh \kappa}(t,z)\,dz,\ \ x\in \mathds R^d, t\in (0,1],
\end{equation}
where $p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$ and $p^y_{\wh \kappa}$ denote the fundamental solutions (i.e.\ heat kernel) associated with
the operators $\LL_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}^y$ and $\LL_{\wh \kappa}^y$, respectively.

We first show that \eqref{l4-4-1} holds for $p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$. Indeed, for every $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ such that $|x-x'|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|&=
\left|\int_0^1 \frac{d}{d \theta}\left(\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}
\left(1,x+\theta(x'-x)\right)\right)\,d\theta\right|\\
&\leqslant |x-x'|\cdot\int_0^1 \left|\nabla^2 p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}
\left(1,x+\theta(x'-x)\right)\right|\,d\theta\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \int_0^1 \left(1+\left|x+\theta(x'-x)\right|\right)^{-d-\alpha(y)-2}\,d\theta\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \left(1+|x|\right)^{-d-\alpha(y)-2},
\end{align*}
where in the third inequality we have used \eqref{p1-1-1}, and the last inequality is due to
the fact that for all $\theta\in [0,1]$ and $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant 1$
\begin{equation*}
\left(1+\left|x+\theta(x'-x)\right|\right)^{-1}\preceq \left(1+|x|\right)^{-1}.
\end{equation*}
Also by \eqref{p1-1-1}, we have that for every
$x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|>1$,
\begin{align*}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|&
\leqslant \big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)\big|+
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|\\
&\preceq (1+|x|)^{-d-\alpha(y)-1}+
(1+|x'|)^{-d-\alpha(y)-1}.
\end{align*}
Combining both estimates above yields that for all $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation}\label{l4-4-3}
\begin{split}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|
\preceq &\left(|x-x'|\wedge 1\right)\left(
(1+|x|)^{-d-\alpha(y)}+
(1+|x'|)^{-d-\alpha(y)}\right).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Since the Markov process $(X_t^{y,{\kappa_1}/{2}})_{t\geqslant0}$ associated with
$ \LL^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$ is a constant time-change of standard rotationally invariant $\alpha(y)$-stable process, by
the scaling property, for all $t>0$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$,
$$
 p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x)= t^{-d/\alpha(y)} p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,t^{-1/\alpha(y)}x).
$$
This along with \eqref{l4-4-3} yields that for all $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$,
\begin{equation}\label{l4-4-4}
\begin{split}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x')\big|
\preceq &\left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\left(
\rho_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}^{y,0}(t,x)+\rho_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}^{y,0}(t,x')\right).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Therefore,  for every $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$,
\begin{align*}
&\left|\nabla p^y(t,x)-\nabla p^y(t,x')\right|\\
&=\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\big(\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x'-z)\big)
\cdot p^y_{\wh \kappa}(t,z)\,dz\right|\\
&\leqslant \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x'-z)\big|
\cdot p^y_{\wh \kappa}(t,z)\,dz\\
&\preceq \left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\cdot
\Bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x-z)\rho^{y,0}_1(t,z)\,dz+\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x'-z)\rho^{y,0}_1(t,z)\,dz\Bigg)\\
&\preceq  \left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\cdot
\left(\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x)
+\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x')\right),
\end{align*}
where the equality above is due to \eqref{l4-4-2}, the second inequality follows from
\eqref{l4-4-4} and \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0}, and in the last inequality we have used
\eqref{l3-2-1-}. By now we have finished the proof.

For simplicity, we assume that $\beta_0< {\alpha_2}/{2}$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$ as before.

(1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. According
to  \eqref{p1-1-3}, for any $\gamma>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{t4-2-1a}
\begin{split}
&\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|\\
&\preceq \big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]\\
&\preceq
\big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}|x-x'|\big)^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge
1}\wedge 1\big]
\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge
1}(t-s)^{-{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+}/{\alpha(z)}}
\times\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}

On the one hand, observing that
$$\frac{\alpha(x)-\gamma}{\alpha(z)}\leqslant 1+\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1}-\frac{\gamma}{\alpha_2}\leqslant
1+\frac{C|x-z|^{\beta_0}}{\alpha_1}-\frac{\gamma}{\alpha_2},$$ we can find a constant
$R_2:=R_2(\alpha,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $x,x',z\in \mathds R^d$ satisfying
$|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|x-z|\leqslant 2R_2$ (which imply that $|x'-z|\leqslant
3R_2$), it holds
\begin{equation*}
\frac{\alpha(x)-\gamma}{\alpha(z)}\leqslant 1-\frac{2\gamma}{3\alpha_2},
\end{equation*}
which in turn yields that for every $0<s\leqslant t\leqslant 1$ and $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant
R_2$ and $|x-z|\leqslant 2R_2$
\begin{align*}
\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|
&\preceq
|x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\left(\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t-s,x'-z)\right).
\end{align*}

On the other hand, when $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|z-x|>2R_2$ (which
imply that $|z-x'|>R_2$), we obtain from \eqref{p1-1-1} and the mean
value theorem that
\begin{align*}
|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)|
&\leqslant |x-x'|\cdot|\nabla p^z(t-s,x-z+\tilde \theta_{x,x',z}(x'-x))|\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \frac{t-s}{((t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)+1}}\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \frac{t-s}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z).
\end{align*}
where in the first inequality $|\tilde \theta_{x,x'z}|\leqslant 1$ is a
constant (which may depend on $x$, $x'$ and $z$), in the second inequality
we have used the fact that
$$|x-z+\tilde \theta_{x,x',z}(x'-x)|\geqslant |x-z|-|x'-x|\geqslant {|x-z|}/{2},$$
and the fourth inequality follows from
$|z-x|>R_2>C(t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}$.

As a result, we obtain that for all $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{equation}\label{pppxy}
\begin{split}
\big|p^z(t,x-z)-p^z(t,x'-z)\big|
&\preceq
|x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\Big(\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t,x-z)
+\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t,x'-z)\Big).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Then, using \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we arrive at for every
$|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\!\cdot\Big[\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})\!+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}\Big)(t,x-y)\!+
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})\!+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}\Big)(t,x'-y)\Big].
\end{align*}

Combining all the estimates together with \eqref{eq2-1} and using again \eqref{pppxy}, we can prove \eqref{t4-2-1} immediately.

(2) Now we assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$.
Replacing $\alpha(x)$ by $\alpha(z)$ in \eqref{t4-2-1a}, we find that for every
$x,x'\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
&\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\wedge 1)(t-s)^{-{(\alpha(z)-\gamma)_+}/{\alpha(z)}} \big(\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big)\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\wedge 1)
\big[\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x'-z)\big].
\end{align*}
Combining this with \eqref{eq2-1}, \eqref{p3-1-2} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, and following the
same arguments above,  we arrive at for all $x,x'\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{align*}
 \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big|
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\\
&\quad\times
\Big[\big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t,x-y)+
\rho^{y,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t,x'-y)\big)\\
&\qquad\,\,+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
\big(\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x'-z)\big)\\
&\qquad \qquad  \times \big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-[{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+{\gamma}/({2\alpha_2})]}+
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-[{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+{\gamma}/({2\alpha_2})]}\Big)(s,z-y)\,dz\, ds \Big]\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}
\big[\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\beta_0/\alpha_2+\gamma_1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\gamma_1}\big)(t,x-y)+
\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\beta_0/\alpha_2+\gamma_1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\gamma_1}\big)(t,x'-y)\big],
\end{align*}
where $\gamma_1:=1-\alpha_2/\alpha_1+\gamma/(2\alpha_2)$. By now we have verified \eqref{t4-2-1aa}. The proof is complete.

(1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. For simplicity, we assume
that $\beta_0< \alpha(x_0)$, and so $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$ and
$\tilde \beta_0(x_0)={\alpha_1\beta_0}/{\alpha(x_0)}$. We will show that we can take the gradient with respect to variable $x$ in the equation \eqref{eq2-1}.
Note that
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^t \left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{t/2}\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{t/2}^t\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)\left(q(s,z,y)-q(s,x_0,y)\right)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{t/2}^t\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\left(\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)-\nabla p^{x_0}(t-s,x_0-z)\right)
q(s,x_0,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&=:\int_0^{t/2}\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_1(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds+\int_{t/2}^t
\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_2(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds+\int_{t/2}^t
\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_3(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds.
\end{align*}



According to \eqref{p1-1-1},
\begin{equation}\label{t5-1-3}
\begin{split}
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|&\preceq \frac{t}{(t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)+1}}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Observing that
\begin{equation*}
\Big|\frac{1}{\alpha(z)}-\frac{1}{\alpha(x)}\Big|\leqslant
\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1^2}\leqslant C|x-z|^{\beta_0},
\end{equation*}
we find by \eqref{t5-1-3} that for every (small enough) $\gamma>0$, there is a constant $R_1:=R_1(\alpha, \kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{t5-1-4}\begin{split}
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|&\preceq
\begin{cases}
\rho^{z,0}_{1-({1}/{\alpha(z)})}(t,x-z),\ &|x-z|\leqslant R_1,\\
\frac{t}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1+1}}
,\ & |x-z|>R_1
\end{cases}\\
&\preceq \rho^{z,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x)})-\gamma}(t,x-z). \end{split}
\end{equation}

Thus, choosing $\gamma>0$ small enough such that $\gamma<\beta_0/\alpha_2$, and using \eqref{l3-2-0}, \eqref{p3-1-1} and
\eqref{t5-1-4}, we can find that
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^{t/2}\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_1(s,z)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq
\int_0^{t/2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)
\big(
\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}(s,z-y)+
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\big)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x_0-y)\!\bigg(\!\int_0^{t/2}\!(t\!-\!s)^{-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-\gamma}\! +\!
(t\!-\!s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{-1+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-\gamma}\,ds \bigg)\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-2\gamma}(t,x-y).
\end{align*}

On the other hand, according to \eqref{p3-1-1a}, \eqref{t5-1-4} and the fact that $\beta_0<\alpha(x_0)$, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
 \int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_2(s,z)|\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
\bigg(\rho^{z,\wh \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\tilde\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}
(s,z-y)
\\
&\qquad\qquad
+\rho^{z,\wh \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\tilde\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(s,x_0-y)\bigg)\,dz\,ds\\
&=:\int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}(J_{21}(s,z)+J_{22}(s,z))\,dz\,ds,
\end{align*}
where $\wh \beta_0=\wh \beta_0(\theta):={\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)}/{\alpha(x_0)}$.

Since $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)>1-\alpha(x_0)$, we can choose
$\theta, \gamma>0$ small enough such that $1+(\wh \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma>0$, which along with
\eqref{l3-2-0} yields
\begin{align*}
\int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}J_{21}(s,z)\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x_0-y)\cdot\Big(
\int_{t/2}^t (t-s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{-1+\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}\\
&\quad \quad +(t-s)^{(\wh \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-
(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}\,ds\Big)\\
&\preceq\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{align*}
On the other hand, noting that for $t/2<s\leqslant t$, it holds that
\begin{equation}\label{t5-1-5}
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(s,x_0-y)\preceq
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(t,x_0-y).
\end{equation}
Since $\tilde \beta_0>1-\alpha(x_0)$, by \eqref{l3-1-1} we have
\begin{align*}
 \int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}J_{22}(s,z)\,dz\,ds
&\preceq
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x_0-y)
\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\wh \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1+(\wh \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-(1/\alpha(x_0))+
(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{align*}



According to \eqref{l4-1-1-1} for the case that $|x_0-z|\leqslant R_1$ and \eqref{t5-1-4} for the case
that $|x_0-z|>R_1$), we arrive at that (by changing the constant $\gamma$ properly) for any $t>0$ and $x_0,z\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
\left|\nabla p^{x_0}(t,x_0-z)-\nabla p^z(t,x_0-z)\right|\preceq
\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-1/\alpha(x_0)-\gamma}(t,x_0-z).
\end{align*}
This, along with \eqref{p3-1-1} yields
\begin{align*}
\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_3(s,z)|\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma}(t,x_0-y)\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1+(\beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-1/\alpha(x_0)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y),
\end{align*} where in the last inequality we used the fact that $\beta_0\geqslant\tilde \beta_0(x_0)>1-\alpha(x_0)$.

Combining all estimates together, we obtain that
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds

According to \eqref{eq2-1}, \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{p3-2-1}, we know

It remains to show the continuity of $p$ with respect to space variables.

For $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ and any $\varepsilon>0$

p^{y}(t,x-y)|

\end{align*}
According to \eqref{p1-1-3} and \eqref{l4-1-1}, we can show that

Throughout the proof, we will assume that $\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$ for simplicity.
Noting that $\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy=1$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$, we have
\begin{align*}
\bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|&=\bigg|
\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy\bigg|\\
&\leqslant \int_{\mathds R^d}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&\leqslant \int_{\{|x-y|\leqslant R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&\quad +\int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&=:J_1+J_2,
\end{align*}
where $R_1$ is the constant in Lemma \ref{l4-1}.

On the one hand, \eqref{l4-1-1} yields that
\begin{align*}
J_1& \preceq \int_{\mathds R^d} \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{1-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y)\,dy\preceq t^{(\beta_0/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})},
\end{align*}
where the last inequality follows from the fact that \eqref{l3-1-1-00} holds for $\tilde \rho$.

On the other hand,
\begin{align*}
J_2& \preceq \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\big(\rho^{x,0}_1(t,x-y)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y)\big)\,dy\\
&\preceq \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\bigg(\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg)\,dy\preceq t \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dy \preceq t.
\end{align*}
Combining with both estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we prove \eqref{p4-1-1-e}.


Choosing $\gamma,\theta>0$ small enough such that $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we immediately get \eqref{p4-1-1}.

By using \eqref{l4-1-2}, we can verify that
\begin{align*}
& \delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( \LL^x- \LL^y\big)p^x(s,w)
\big(\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\!\!\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( \LL^x- \LL^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)
\big(\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds.
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{align*}
& \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
& \leqslant \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( \LL^x- \LL^y\big)p^x(s,w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( \LL^x- \LL^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{align*}


According to \eqref{p1-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-5}, for every $\theta \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant
$R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation}\label{l4-2-2}
\begin{split}
&\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\\
&\preceq \big[\left((t-s)^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|w|\right)^{\theta}\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\\
&\quad\times\big[
\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w)
+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big]\\
&\preceq \left(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\right)\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
 \cdot\big[
\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w)\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad
+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Furthermore, following the argument of Lemma \ref{l1-1}, we can derive that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$
\begin{equation}\label{l4-2-3}
\begin{split}
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y \pm z)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz
\preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y),\\
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz
\preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{l4-1-4} with \eqref{l4-2-2} and \eqref{l4-2-3}, we find that for  all $t\in(0,1]$ and  $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{align*}
J_1 &\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot \bigg[
\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad+\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\,dw\,ds\bigg]\\
&=:|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot(J_{11}+J_{12}).
\end{align*}
Since \eqref{l3-2-1-} holds true for $\tilde \rho$ as mentioned in Remark \ref{r3-3}(2),
for every $0<\theta<\alpha_1$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\alpha_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1}))/2)$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{l4-2-3a}
\begin{split}
J_{11}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,x-y) \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\big(s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}(t-s)^{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}
+s^{-\gamma}(t-s)^{-1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\big)\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,x-y) \bigg(t^{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\int_0^{{t}/{2}}s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}\,ds+
t^{-1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\int_0^{{t}/{2}} s^{-\gamma}\,ds\bigg)\\
& \preceq  \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
On the other hand, note that for every $0<s<{t}/{2}$, $$\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).$$
Then, it holds that
\begin{align*}
J_{12}&\preceq  \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y)\cdot
\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\,dw\,ds\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y),
\end{align*} where \eqref{l3-1-1-00} was used in the last inequality.
Hence, we find that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
J_1 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{equation*}

By estimates for
 the terms
$$\big|\big( \LL^x- \LL^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|$$ and $$\big|
\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|,$$ we can deal with the singularity
as $s$ near $t$ by the same arguments above and obtain that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
J_2 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{equation*}


Combining both of the estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we finally obtain that \eqref{l4-2-1} holds true.

proof.raw:
(i) We first assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
We will prove that $p(t,x,y)$ constructed by \eqref{eq2-1} satisfies all the assertions.

According to Proposition \ref{t4-1}, \eqref{t1-1-1} holds. By
Propositions \ref{p3-2} and \ref{p3-3}, \eqref{t1-1-4} and \eqref{t1-1-4a} hold true.
Propositions \ref{t4-2} and \ref{t5-1} imply
\eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-7a}, respectively. By Proposition \ref{p4-5},  we know that
$p:(0,1]\times\mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d\rightarrow \mathds R_+$ is continuous. The lower bounds
\eqref{t1-1-4b}  will be shown in Corollary \ref{c-lower}, which is a consequence of Propositions
\ref{p4-3} and \ref{t4-4} in the next subsection.

\smallskip

(ii) According to  the proof of Proposition \ref{t4-1}, we can
obtain that for every $ \varepsilon \in (0,1)$, there exist a constant
$C( \varepsilon)>0$ and a measurable function $\eta:\mathds R^d \to  \mathds R_+$ such that
$\int_{\mathds R^d}\eta(y)\,dy<\infty$,

\begin{equation*}
\sup_{t \in ( \varepsilon,1)}\Big|\frac{\partial p(t,x,y)}{\partial t}\Big|\leqslant C( \varepsilon)\eta(x-y)
\end{equation*} and
\begin{equation*}\begin{split}
&\sup_{t \in ( \varepsilon,1),\sigma>0}\bigg|\int_{\{|z|>\sigma\}}\big(p(t,x+z,y)+p(t,x-z,y)-2p(t,x,y)\big)
\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg|\leqslant C( \varepsilon)\eta(x-y).\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Thus, by the dominated convergence theorem, it is easy to verify
that $\LL u_f (t, \cdot) (x)$ exists for each $t>0$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, $t\mapsto \LL u_f (t, \cdot) (x)$
is continuous,  and that \eqref{t1-1-2} holds.

\smallskip

(iii) We have by \eqref{eq2-1} that
\begin{align*}
u_f(t,x)-f(x)&=\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\big(f(y)-f(x)\big)\,dy+
f(x)\left(\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\right)\\
&\quad +\int_{\mathds R^d} f(y)\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\,dy\\
&=:J_1+J_2+J_3.
\end{align*}

For any $f\in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$ and for every $ \varepsilon>0$, there exists
a constant $\delta:=\delta( \varepsilon)>0$ such that $|f(x)-f(y)|< \varepsilon$ for all $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with
$|x-y|\leqslant \delta$. Thus,
\begin{align*}
|J_1|&\leqslant \int_{\{|y-x|\leqslant \delta\}}p^y(t,x-y)|f(y)-f(x)|\,dy+
\int_{\{|y-x|>\delta\}}p^y(t,x-y)|f(y)-f(x)|\,dy\\
&\leqslant  \varepsilon \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y)\,dy+
C( \varepsilon)\|f\|_{\infty}\int_{\{|y-x|>\delta\}}\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dy\leqslant C \varepsilon+C( \varepsilon,\delta)t,
\end{align*}
where in the last inequality we have used \eqref{l3-1-1}.
According to \eqref{p4-1-1}, it holds that $\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}|J_2|=0$.
Furthermore, by \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, we obtain that for $\gamma<\beta_0^*/{\alpha_2}$ with $\beta^*\in (0,\beta]\cap(0,\alpha_2/2)$,
\begin{align*}
|J_3|&\preceq \|f\|_{\infty}\Bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}
\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{{(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)}-\gamma}(s,z-y)+ \rho^{y,\beta_0^*}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\Big)\,dz\,ds\,dy\Bigg]\\
&\preceq \|f\|_{\infty}\int_{\mathds R^d}
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{1+{(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)}-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0^*}_{1-\gamma}\Big)(t,x-y)\,dy\preceq t^{{(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)}-\gamma}\|f\|_{\infty}.
\end{align*}
Combining all the estimates above together, we arrive at
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}\big|u_f(t,x)-f(x)\big|\leqslant  \varepsilon.
\end{equation*}
Since $ \varepsilon$ is arbitrary, we know that \eqref{t1-1-3} holds.

\smallskip

(iv) Denote by $C_{b}^{\varepsilon}(\mathds R^d)$ the set of bounded H\"{o}lder continuous functions, and by $C_{b}^{2,\varepsilon}(\mathds R^d)$ the set of bounded twice differentiable functions whose second derivatives are uniformly H\"{o}lder continuous.  We first suppose that $f \in C_{b}^{2,\varepsilon}(\mathds R^d)$. Let
\begin{equation*}
\tilde u_f(t,x):=f(x)+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}p(s,x,y)\LL f(y)\,dy\,ds=f(x)+\int_0^t
u_{\LL f}(s,x)\,ds.
\end{equation*}
Since $\LL f \in C_{b}^{\varepsilon}(\mathds R^d)$, it is easy to see that
\begin{equation*}
\frac{\partial \tilde u_f(t,x)}{\partial t}=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)\LL f(y)\,dy
=u_{\LL f}(t,x),\quad t\in (0,1]
\end{equation*} and
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x\in\mathds R^d}|\tilde u_f(t,x)-f(x)|=0.
\end{equation*}

On the other hand, due to $\LL f \in C_{b}^{\varepsilon}(\mathds R^d)$ again, it follows from \eqref{t1-1-2} that
$ \LL u_{\LL f}(t,x)=\frac{\partial u_{\LL f}(t,x)}{\partial t}$. Furthermore, following the
proof of Proposition \ref{t4-1}, we will get
\begin{align*}
\int_0^t \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d} \LL^x p^z(t-s,x-z)\LL f(z)\,dz\Big|\,ds
&\leqslant \int_0^t \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d} \LL^z p^z(t-s,x-z)\LL f(z)\,dz\Big|\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_0^t \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d}( \LL^x- \LL^z) p^z(t-s,x-z)\LL f(z)\,dz\Big|\,ds<\infty
\end{align*} and so $$\int_0^t \LL u_{\LL f}(s,x)\,ds$$ is well defined.
Hence,
\begin{align*}
\LL\tilde u_f(t,x)&=\LL f(x)+\int_0^t
 \LL u_{\LL f}(s,x)\,ds=\LL f(x)+\int_0^t \frac{\partial u_{\LL f}(s,x)}{\partial s}\,ds\\
&=\LL f(x)+u_{\LL f}(t,x)-\LL f(x)=u_{\LL f}(t,x),
\end{align*}
where in the third equality we used
$\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x\in\mathds R^d}|u_{\LL f}(t,x)-\LL f(x)|=0$, thanks to \eqref{t1-1-3}.
Therefore, both $u_f$ and $\tilde u_f$ are solutions of the following PDE
\begin{equation}\label{t1-1-11}
\begin{cases}
\frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t}= \LL u(t,x),\\
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}|u(t,x)-f(x)|=0.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}

Let $w_f(t,x):=u_f(t,x)-\tilde u_f(t,x)$. Then,  \eqref{t4-3-2a} and \eqref{t4-3-1} hold for $w_f$ with $w_f(0,x)\equiv 0$. At the same time, it is easy to verify from \eqref{eq2-1}
that the function $t \mapsto \LL w_f(t,x)$ is continuous on $(0,1]$, and that
\eqref{t1-1-7} implies \eqref{t4-3-2} holds for $w_f$. Thus, by Theorem \ref{t4-3}, we have
\begin{equation*}
w_f(t,x)\leqslant w_f(0,x)=0,\quad (t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d.
\end{equation*}
Furthermore, applying the argument above to $-w_f$, we finally get that \begin{equation*}
w_f(t,x)\equiv 0,\quad  (t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d.
\end{equation*}
Therefore, $u_f(t,x)=\tilde u_f(t,x)$ for any $t \in (0,1]$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$, which further implies that
\begin{equation*}
\int_{\mathds R^d} \LL p(t,\cdot,y)(x)f(y)\,dy=\frac{\partial u_f(t,x)}{\partial t}
=\frac{\partial \tilde u_{f}(t,x)}{\partial t}=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)\LL f(y)\,dy.
\end{equation*}
Thus, \eqref{t1-1-5a} holds. Observe that
\begin{equation*}
u_f(t,x)=\tilde u_f(t,x)=f(x)+\int_0^t u_{\LL f}(s,x)\,ds.
\end{equation*}
According to \eqref{t1-1-3}, we arrive at \eqref{t1-1-5b} immediately.
By the standard approximation procedure, we know that \eqref{t1-1-5a} and
\eqref{t1-1-5b} still hold for every $f \in C_{b,u}^2(\mathds R^d)$.

\smallskip

(v) Let $u(t,x)=:\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)\,dy$. Then, according to \eqref{t1-1-2} and \eqref{t1-1-3}, we know that
$u$ satisfies the following equation
\begin{equation}\label{t1-1-11}
\begin{cases}
\frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t}= \LL u(t,x),\\
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}\big|u(t,x)-1\big|=0.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
At the same time, $v(t,x)\equiv 1$ satisfies the equation \eqref{t1-1-11} above. Note that \eqref{t4-3-2} and the time continuity condition hold for both
$u(t,x)$ and $v(t,x)$. Then, using the same argument as in (iv)  and applying Theorem \ref{t4-3}, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)\,dy=u(t,x)=1,\quad (t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d,
\end{equation*}
which is \eqref{t1-1-6}.

For every fixed $s \in (0,1)$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, we define $$u_{s,y}(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,z)p(s,z,y)\,dz.$$
 Again by \eqref{t1-1-2} and \eqref{t1-1-3}, the following equation holds for $u_{s,y}$:
\begin{equation}\label{t1-1-12}
\begin{cases}
\frac{\partial u_{s,y}(t,x)}{\partial t}= \LL u_{s,y}(t,x),\\
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}|u_{s,y}(t,x)-p(s,x,y)|=0.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
On the other hand, it is easy to verify that $v_{s,y}(t,x):=p(t+s,x,y)$ satisfies
\eqref{t1-1-12}, and \eqref{t4-3-2} and the time continuity condition hold for both
$u_{s,y}(t,x)$ and $v_{s,y}(t,x)$.  Following the procedure above and applying Theorem \ref{t4-3}, we arrive at
$$\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,z)p(s,z,y)\,dz=u_{s,y}(t,x)=v_{s,y}(t,x)=p(t+s,x,y),$$
which is \eqref{t1-1-5}.

\smallskip

(vi)
Suppose that $\wh p(t,x,y)$ is another
jointly continuous function  on $(0, 1]\times \mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d$
that is bounded for each $t>0$ and
 satisfies  \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-2a}-\eqref{t1-1-3}.
For every $f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$, let
$$\wh u_f(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}\wh p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy \quad \hbox{and} \quad
\wh w_f(t,x):=u_f(t,x)-\wh u_f(t,x).
$$
 Then both $u_f$ and $\wh u_f$ satisfy \eqref{t1-1-2}. By the same argument above, we have
$\wh w_f(t,x)=0$ for each $(t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d$. This implies
that for every $f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$,
\begin{equation*}
\int_{\mathds R^d} p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy=\int_{\mathds R^d} \wh p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy.
\end{equation*}
Consequently, $p(t,x,y)=\wh p(t,x,y)$ for a.e.\ $y \in \mathds R^d$ and hence for every $y\in \mathds R^d$.

\smallskip

(vii) Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$.  The desired upper and lower estimates and the regularity can be proved in a similar way as before. On the other hand, the condition ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<\beta_*/\alpha_2<{1}/{2}$ implies that
$\alpha_2-\alpha_1<{\alpha_1}/{2}<1$, which ensures that
\eqref{t4-3-2} holds with $u_f(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy$ for every
$f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$. Therefore, following the arguments in steps (i)-(vi), we can verify that \eqref{t1-1-5}-\eqref{t1-1-5b} hold in such case.

remark.raw:
\label{remark1}
\begin{itemize}
\item [(1)] From \eqref{t1-1-4} and \eqref{t1-1-4b}, we know that both upper and lower bounds of
near-diagonal
estimates for $p(t,x,y)$ enjoy the same order $t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}$, which typically depends on $x$.
In particular, along with \eqref{t1-1-4b}, when $r_0=\infty$ in \eqref{t1-1-4a} (i.e.\ $\alpha(x)\equiv \alpha \in (0,2)$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$), we arrive at the two-sided heat kernel estimates obtained in
\cite{CZ}.
Furthermore, by \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-7a}, the regularity of $p(t,\cdot,y)$ at $x=x_0$ only depends on
$x_0$.

\item [(2)] Compared with these results yielded by  Duhamel's formula in \cite{Kol},  Theorem \ref{t1-1}(v) shows that the function $u_f(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy$ solves  the Cauchy problem for  $\LL$. In particular, by \eqref{t1-1-1} and \eqref{t1-1-3}, we have
\begin{equation*}
\begin{cases}
\frac{\partial }{\partial t} p(t,x,y) = \LL p(t,\cdot,y)(x)\\
\lim_{t \downarrow 0} p(t,x,y)=\delta_y(x),
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}
which means that $p(t,x,y)$ is the fundamental solution associated
with $\LL$. It is easy to deduce from \eqref{t1-1-7},  \eqref{t1-1-5}, \eqref{t1-1-6},
\eqref{t1-1-2} and \eqref{t1-1-5a} that there is  a conservative Feller process  having the strong Feller property
associated with the operator $\LL$;  cf.  Proposition \ref{p4-4} below.
Recall that a Markov process on $\mathds R^d$ is said to be a Feller process if its transition semigroup is a strongly continuous semigroup in the Banach space of continuous functions that vanish at infinity equipped
with the uniform norm.
A Markov process is said to have the strong Feller property if its transition semigroup maps bounded
measurable functions to bounded continuous functions.
\end{itemize}

Background
Non-local operators  arise naturally in the study of stochastic processes with jumps. Various properties of the non-local operator $\LL$ have been intensively investigated both from the analytic and the probabilistic point of view.

We first recall some known results for the constant order case,
i.e.\ $\alpha(x) \equiv \alpha \in (0,2)$ for all $x\in\mathds R^d$. The regularity
properties of the operator $\LL$ including the H\"{o}lder continuity
of harmonic functions, the Schauder estimates and the $L^p$
estimates were studied in \cite{Bass2,CS1,CS,CV,CRZ,S1,S2,Z}. When
the operator $\LL$ is symmetric with respect to the Lebesgue measure,
existence and two-sided estimates of the heat kernel associated with $\LL$
were obtained in \cite{CK,CK1}, and
the corresponding parabolic Harnack inequality was also established
there. For general $\kappa(x,z)$ satisfying \eqref{e1-2}, the associated
heat kernel was constructed by Levi's method in \cite{CZ}, where the
corresponding two-sided estimates and gradient estimates were given,
and the parabolic equation (see \eqref{t1-1-1} below) was also
verified. Recently the extension of \cite{CZ}
from the L\'evy kernel $1/|z|^{d+\alpha}$ to that of a  class of subordinate Brownian motion
was presented in  \cite{KSV}. See also
\cite{BSK, GS, Kim, KK1,KK2, Ku, KR17,Kul, SZ} for the construction of certain L\'evy
type processes via Levi's  (parametrix)
 method. Besides, existence and uniqueness
(i.e.\ well-posedness) of the martingale problem for $\LL$ were proved
in \cite{BT, CZ4, J} under some mild continuous conditions on $\kappa(x,z)$.

When the index function $\alpha(x)$ depends on $x $ and the jump
coefficient $\kappa(x,z)=\frac{\alpha(x)2^{\alpha(x)-1}\Gamma
((\alpha(x)+d)/2)}{\pi^{d/2}\,\Gamma(1-(\alpha(x)/2))}$ for all
$x,z\in \mathds R^d$, $\LL$ can be written as a pseudo-differential operator
$-p(x,D)$ with the symbol $p(x, \xi)= -|\xi|^{\alpha(x)}$; that is,
$$
\LL f(x) = \frac{1}{(2\pi)^d} \int_{\mathds R^d} e^{\langle ix, \xi\rangle} p(x, \xi) \wh  f(\xi)\, d\xi
= \frac{1}{(2\pi)^d} \int_{\mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d} e^{i \langle x-y, \xi\rangle} p(x, \xi) f(y) \,dy \,d\xi .
$$
Formally, we can write $\LL$ as $-(-\Delta)^{\alpha (x)/2}$.
For this reason, we call $\alpha(x)$ the order of the non-local operator at the point $x\in \mathds R^d$.
Existence and well-posedness of
the martingale solution for $\LL= -(-\Delta)^{\alpha (x)/2}$ were established in Bass \cite{Bass1}, which
immediately yields that there is  a strong Markov process corresponding to $-(-\Delta)^{\alpha (x)/2}$.
(This process was called the stable-like process in \cite{Bass1}). A few
properties for such stable-like process (including existence of heat
kernel, sample path properties and the long-time behaviors) have
been investigated in \cite{BSW,Hoh,KN,Neg,NS, Sch} by using the theory of
pseudo-differential operators and Fourier analysis. When $\kappa (x,
z)=\kappa (x)$ is independent of $z$ and both $\alpha (x)$ and
$\kappa (x)$ have uniformly bounded continuous derivatives, the heat
kernel for $\LL$ was constructed formally in \cite[Section 5]{Kol} via
 Duhamel's formula, and some upper bound estimates for heat kernel were
also given there. Duhamel's formula has also been adopted in
\cite{CW,W} to study the foundational solution to fractional
Laplacian or Laplacian perturbed by non-local operators. We also
mention that there are some results for the case that $\kappa(x,z)$
depends on $z$. For instance, the regularity for harmonic functions
or the semigroups associated with $\LL$ were studied in
\cite{BK1,LW,S1}, and the elliptic Harnack inequality was obtained
in \cite{BK2}.

From all the results mentioned above, we can see that there are
already a lot of developments related to   non-local operators of
variable order. However, the following questions, which should be
fundamental and interesting, were still unknown.
\begin{itemize}
\item [(1)] When $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant, how can we construct a fundamental solution of $\LL$ that really satisfies
 the parabolic equation \eqref{t1-1-1} below?  What are upper
and lower bound estimates for this solution (if it exists)? We point out that it had not been established that,
even under additional smoothness assumptions on $\alpha (x)$ and $\kappa (x)$,
the  heat kernel constructed  in \cite{Kol}  by Duhamel formula is actually a solution to the equation \eqref{t1-1-1}.

\item[(2)] When $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant and $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$, is there a strong Markov process
associated with $\LL$?  In literature, the existence of strong Markov process was
always assumed a priori  in the study of regularity of harmonic
functions and elliptic Harnack inequalities for such non-local operator $\LL$,
see \cite{BK1,BK2, LW} for examples.

\item[(3)] In existing literature,
  regularity for the solution to parabolic equation \eqref{t1-1-1} associated
with $\LL$ usually depends on
 the uniform bounds $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$ in
\eqref{e1-3}.
Can one establish regularity of the fundamental solution in some neighborhood of  $x_0$ (such  as  gradient estimate) in terms of $\alpha(x_0)$ under some special settings?
\end{itemize}

In the remainder of this paper, we denote nabla p^y(t,cdot)(x) by nabla p^y(t,x) for simplicity. (1) We first consider the case that kappa(x,z) is independent of z. Let R_1:=R_1(alpha,kappa,gamma) be a positive constant to be determined later. The proof is split into the following five different cases. Case (a): |x-x'|>R_1. By and the condition beta_0>alpha_2theta, it holds that |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)| &leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)|+|q_0(t,x',y)|preceq rho_-gamma^y,beta_0(t,x-y)+rho_-gamma^y,beta_0(t,x'-y)\\ &preceq big(|x-x'|^alpha_1(beta_0-alpha_2theta)/alpha(x)wedge1big)big(rho_-gamma^y,beta_0(t,x-y)+rho_-gamma^y,beta_0(t,x'-y)big). full.raw:
Background
Non-local operators  arise naturally in the study of stochastic processes with jumps. Various properties of the non-local operator $\LL$ have been intensively investigated both from the analytic and the probabilistic point of view.

We first recall some known results for the constant order case,
i.e.\ $\alpha(x) \equiv \alpha \in (0,2)$ for all $x\in\mathds R^d$. The regularity
properties of the operator $\LL$ including the H\"{o}lder continuity
of harmonic functions, the Schauder estimates and the $L^p$
estimates were studied in \cite{Bass2,CS1,CS,CV,CRZ,S1,S2,Z}. When
the operator $\LL$ is symmetric with respect to the Lebesgue measure,
existence and two-sided estimates of the heat kernel associated with $\LL$
were obtained in \cite{CK,CK1}, and
the corresponding parabolic Harnack inequality was also established
there. For general $\kappa(x,z)$ satisfying \eqref{e1-2}, the associated
heat kernel was constructed by Levi's method in \cite{CZ}, where the
corresponding two-sided estimates and gradient estimates were given,
and the parabolic equation (see \eqref{t1-1-1} below) was also
verified. Recently the extension of \cite{CZ}
from the L\'evy kernel $1/|z|^{d+\alpha}$ to that of a  class of subordinate Brownian motion
was presented in  \cite{KSV}. See also
\cite{BSK, GS, Kim, KK1,KK2, Ku, KR17,Kul, SZ} for the construction of certain L\'evy
type processes via Levi's  (parametrix)
 method. Besides, existence and uniqueness
(i.e.\ well-posedness) of the martingale problem for $\LL$ were proved
in \cite{BT, CZ4, J} under some mild continuous conditions on $\kappa(x,z)$.

When the index function $\alpha(x)$ depends on $x $ and the jump
coefficient $\kappa(x,z)=\frac{\alpha(x)2^{\alpha(x)-1}\Gamma
((\alpha(x)+d)/2)}{\pi^{d/2}\,\Gamma(1-(\alpha(x)/2))}$ for all
$x,z\in \mathds R^d$, $\LL$ can be written as a pseudo-differential operator
$-p(x,D)$ with the symbol $p(x, \xi)= -|\xi|^{\alpha(x)}$; that is,
$$
\LL f(x) = \frac{1}{(2\pi)^d} \int_{\mathds R^d} e^{\langle ix, \xi\rangle} p(x, \xi) \wh  f(\xi)\, d\xi
= \frac{1}{(2\pi)^d} \int_{\mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d} e^{i \langle x-y, \xi\rangle} p(x, \xi) f(y) \,dy \,d\xi .
$$
Formally, we can write $\LL$ as $-(-\Delta)^{\alpha (x)/2}$.
For this reason, we call $\alpha(x)$ the order of the non-local operator at the point $x\in \mathds R^d$.
Existence and well-posedness of
the martingale solution for $\LL= -(-\Delta)^{\alpha (x)/2}$ were established in Bass \cite{Bass1}, which
immediately yields that there is  a strong Markov process corresponding to $-(-\Delta)^{\alpha (x)/2}$.
(This process was called the stable-like process in \cite{Bass1}). A few
properties for such stable-like process (including existence of heat
kernel, sample path properties and the long-time behaviors) have
been investigated in \cite{BSW,Hoh,KN,Neg,NS, Sch} by using the theory of
pseudo-differential operators and Fourier analysis. When $\kappa (x,
z)=\kappa (x)$ is independent of $z$ and both $\alpha (x)$ and
$\kappa (x)$ have uniformly bounded continuous derivatives, the heat
kernel for $\LL$ was constructed formally in \cite[Section 5]{Kol} via
 Duhamel's formula, and some upper bound estimates for heat kernel were
also given there. Duhamel's formula has also been adopted in
\cite{CW,W} to study the foundational solution to fractional
Laplacian or Laplacian perturbed by non-local operators. We also
mention that there are some results for the case that $\kappa(x,z)$
depends on $z$. For instance, the regularity for harmonic functions
or the semigroups associated with $\LL$ were studied in
\cite{BK1,LW,S1}, and the elliptic Harnack inequality was obtained
in \cite{BK2}.

From all the results mentioned above, we can see that there are
already a lot of developments related to   non-local operators of
variable order. However, the following questions, which should be
fundamental and interesting, were still unknown.
\begin{itemize}
\item [(1)] When $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant, how can we construct a fundamental solution of $\LL$ that really satisfies
 the parabolic equation \eqref{t1-1-1} below?  What are upper
and lower bound estimates for this solution (if it exists)? We point out that it had not been established that,
even under additional smoothness assumptions on $\alpha (x)$ and $\kappa (x)$,
the  heat kernel constructed  in \cite{Kol}  by Duhamel formula is actually a solution to the equation \eqref{t1-1-1}.

\item[(2)] When $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant and $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$, is there a strong Markov process
associated with $\LL$?  In literature, the existence of strong Markov process was
always assumed a priori  in the study of regularity of harmonic
functions and elliptic Harnack inequalities for such non-local operator $\LL$,
see \cite{BK1,BK2, LW} for examples.

\item[(3)] In existing literature,
  regularity for the solution to parabolic equation \eqref{t1-1-1} associated
with $\LL$ usually depends on
 the uniform bounds $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$ in
\eqref{e1-3}.
Can one establish regularity of the fundamental solution in some neighborhood of  $x_0$ (such  as  gradient estimate) in terms of $\alpha(x_0)$ under some special settings?
\end{itemize}

\item[(1)] According to Theorem \ref{t1-2} above, when $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant function and $\kappa(x,z)$

for the existence of a strong Markov process (in fact a Feller process having the strong Feller property)
associated with $\LL$

strong Markov process is required and assumed a prior in the proofs of
the H\"{o}lder continuity of harmonic functions in \cite{BK1} and
the elliptic Harnack inequality for $\LL$ in \cite{BK2}.

 \end{enumerate}

We conclude this part with the following remarks on some possible extensions of Theorems \ref{t1-1} and \ref{t1-2}.


\begin{remark}\label{rrr-000}
\begin{itemize}
 \item[(1)] By carefully checking the arguments of Theorem \ref{t1-1}, one can see that Theorem \ref{t1-1} still holds true if the condition that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$ is replaced  by the following two assumptions on $\kappa(x,z)$:
\begin{itemize}
\item [(i)] For every fixed $x \in \mathds R^d$, $\kappa(x,\cdot):\mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+$
is a radial function, i.e., $\kappa(x,z)$ only depends on $|z|$.

\item [(ii)] Let $j(x,r)=\wt \kappa(x,r)r^{-d-\alpha(x)}$ for $x \in \mathds R^d$ and $r>0$, where
$\wt \kappa(x,r):=\kappa(x,z)$ with $|z|=r$. For every $x \in \mathds R^d$, $j(x,\cdot)$ is non-increasing and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ such that the function $r\mapsto -\frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial j(x,r)}{\partial r}$ is non-increasing.
\end{itemize}

\item[(2)] Let $\wt \LL f(x)=\LL f(x)+\langle b(x), \nabla f(x)\rangle$, where $b:\mathds R^d\rightarrow \mathds R^d$ is bounded and uniformly
H\"older continuous.
It is possible to extend Theorems \ref{t1-1} and \ref{t1-2}  to $\wt \LL$ under the assumption that $\alpha_1>1$,
When $\alpha_1>1$, the gradient perturbation $\langle b(x), \nabla \rangle$ is of lower order than $\LL$.
We  refer the readers to
\cite{BJ, CD, CH, JS, MM, MM1,XZ}
on heat kernel estimates associated
with non-local operators under gradient perturbation.
For heat kernel estimates associated
with non-local operators under non-local perturbations, see \cite{CW, W, CHXZ}.


\item[(3)] By combining with the approach from \cite{CZ4},
it is possible to remove the symmetry assumption of $\kappa (x, z)$ in $z$.
But we will not pursue this extension  in this paper.

\end{itemize}
\end{remark}

\begin{proof} Without loss of generality, throughout this proof we will assume that $2\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$; otherwise, we will replace $\beta_0$ by $\beta_0^{**}\in (0,\beta_0]\cap (0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ For simplicity, we only verify the case that $c_0=1$.

(i) We first consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
Note that $$p^z(t,x-z)\preceq \rho_1^{z,0}(t,x-z),\quad t\in (0,1],x,z\in \mathds R^d.$$ This, along with
\eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, yields that for every $(t,x,y)\in
(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$ and {any constant
$0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2},$}
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d} p^z(t-s,x-
z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\preceq
\big(\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+
\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big).
\end{equation*}
Therefore, $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and
\begin{equation}\label{p3-2-3}
p(t,x,y)\preceq \Big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+
\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\Big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq
\big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big).
\end{equation}

When $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha_2}}$,
$$\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-\gamma}|x-y|^{\beta_0}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)
\preceq t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big).$$
Hence, due to $\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we get
\begin{equation}\label{p3-2-3a}
\begin{split}
p(t,x,y)\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(y)}}\preceq
t^{-{d}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where the third inequality follows from \eqref{l3-2-8}.

Next, we will verify the other two cases in the upper bound \eqref{p3-2-1}. Observe that
for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ such that
$|x-y|\leqslant 1$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
 \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}
&=
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{({1/\alpha(y)})-({1/\alpha(x)})}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}
 \preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&\preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}})^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&=t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|(d+\alpha(y))}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}}\\
&\preceq t^{-{(d+\alpha_2)|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot
t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1}}\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}} \preceq
\frac{t^{-C_1R_0^{\beta_0}}}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality we used
$t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant 1$, and the third inequality follows from the fact that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\preceq t^{-{|\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)|}/{\alpha(x)}}.
\end{align*}
Thus, choosing $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\gamma)$ small enough  such that
$C_1R_0^{\beta_0}<\gamma$ and using the definition of $\rho^{x,0}_0$, we can
get that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with
$|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{equation}\label{l4-1-5}
\rho^{y,0}_0(t,z)\preceq t^{-\gamma}\rho^{x,0}_0(t,z).
\end{equation}
By the definition of \eqref{e3-0}, we know immediately that \eqref{l4-1-5} still holds for
every $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|> 1$. This is, \eqref{l4-1-5} holds for all $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$.

Hence, combining \eqref{p3-2-3}, \eqref{p3-2-3a} with \eqref{l4-1-5} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we find that
\begin{align*}
p(t,x,y)&\preceq
 \big(\rho^{y,0}_{1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}
\big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq \begin{cases}t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, & |y-x|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\
\frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},& t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |y-x|\leqslant R_0,\\
\frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x|> R_0.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}

(ii) If there are some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such
that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then for
every $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$ and $z \in
B(y,{r_0}/{2})$,
$
\alpha(z)=\alpha(y)=\alpha(x_0).
$
Hence, by \eqref{p3-1-2b}, we have
\begin{equation*}
|q(t,x,y)|\preceq
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_0\Big)(t,x-y)\quad\textrm{ for all }
x\in \mathds R^d\textrm{ and }y \in B\big(x_0,{r_0}/{2}\big).
\end{equation*}
Based on the inequality above, the computation in part (i) is valid
with $\gamma=0$ for $x=x_0$ and $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$, which
proves \eqref{p3-2-2} for the case that $y \in
B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$. The upper bound for the case
$|y-x_0|>{r_0}/{2}$ is just the same as that of \eqref{p3-2-1}.


(iii) If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and
${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, then, according to
\eqref{p3-1-2}, we know that the computation in part (i) holds with
$\gamma$ replaced by $\tilde\gamma$. Thus, following the argument in part
(i), we can obtain \eqref{p3-2-1a}. Similarly as in (ii),
\eqref{p3-2-2a} could be verified by using \eqref{p3-1-2c}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The estimate \eqref{p3-2-2} indicates that if $\alpha(x)$ is a
constant $\alpha\in(0,2)$ locally, then we can get a upper bound for
$p(t,x,y)$ which is also locally comparable with that for the heat
kernel of rotationally symmetric $\alpha$-stable process.  In particular, when
$\alpha(x)\equiv\alpha$ for all $x \in \mathds R^d$, \eqref{p3-2-2a} coincides with
the upper bound given in \cite[Therem 1.1]{CZ}.
\end{remark}

Besides Proposition \ref{p3-2}, we also can obtain the following upper bound for $p(t,x,y)$, which is based on Proposition \ref{P-new}.

Noting that $\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy=1$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$, we have

\bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|&=\bigg|
\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy\bigg|\\
&\leqslant \int_{\mathds R^d}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&\leqslant \int_{\{|x-y|\leqslant R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&\quad +\int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&=:J_1+J_2,
\end{align*}
where $R_1$ is the constant in Lemma \ref{l4-1}.

On the one hand, \eqref{l4-1-1} yields that
\begin{align*}
J_1& \preceq \int_{\mathds R^d} \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{1-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y)\,dy\preceq t^{(\beta_0/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})},
\end{align*}

&\preceq \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\bigg(\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg)\,dy\preceq t \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dy \preceq t.
\end{align*}
Combining with both estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we prove \eqref{p4-1-1-e}.


Choosing $\gamma,\theta>0$ small enough such that $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we immediately get \eqref{p4-1-1}.
\end{proof}

By using \eqref{l4-1-2}, we can verify that
\begin{align*}
& \delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( \LL^x- \LL^y\big)p^x(s,w)
\big(\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\!\!\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( \LL^x- \LL^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)
\big(\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds.
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{align*}
& \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
& \leqslant \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( \LL^x- \LL^y\big)p^x(s,w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( \LL^x- \LL^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{align*}


According to \eqref{p1-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-5}, for every $\theta \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant
$R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation}\label{l4-2-2}
\begin{split}
&\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\\
&\preceq \big[\left((t-s)^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|w|\right)^{\theta}\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\\

\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w)
+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big]\\
&\preceq \left(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\right)\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
 \cdot\big[
\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w)\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad
+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Furthermore, following the argument of Lemma \ref{l1-1}, we can derive that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$
\begin{equation}\label{l4-2-3}
\begin{split}
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y \pm z)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz
\preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y),\\
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz
\preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{l4-1-4} with \eqref{l4-2-2} and \eqref{l4-2-3}, we find that for  all $t\in(0,1]$ and  $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{align*}

&\qquad\qquad\qquad+\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\,dw\,ds\bigg]\\

Since \eqref{l3-2-1-} holds true for $\tilde \rho$ as mentioned in Remark \ref{r3-3}(2),

\end{equation}

\begin{align*}

\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\,dw\,ds\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y),
\end{align*} where \eqref{l3-1-1-00} was used in the last inequality.
Hence, we find that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
J_1 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).

By estimates for

$$\big|\big( \LL^x- \LL^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|$$ and $$\big|
\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|,$$ we can deal with the singularity

\begin{equation*}

\end{equation*}


Combining both of the estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we finally obtain that \eqref{l4-2-1} holds true.

In particular, along with , when r_0=infty in (i.e.\ alpha(x)equiv alpha in (0,2) for all xin mathds R^d), we arrive at the two-sided heat kernel estimates obtained in . Furthermore, by and , the regularity of p(t,cdot,y) at x=x_0 only depends on x_0. item [(2)] Compared with these results yielded by Duhamel's formula in , Theorem (v) shows that the function u_f(t,x):=int_mathds R^dp(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy solves the Cauchy problem for LL. In particular, by and , we have fracpartial partial t p(t,x,y) = LL p(t,cdot,y)(x)\\ lim_t downarrow 0 p(t,x,y)=delta_y(x), which means that p(t,x,y) is the fundamental solution associated with LL. It is easy to deduce from , , , and that there is a conservative Feller process having the strong Feller property associated with the operator LL; cf. Proposition below. Recall that a Markov process on mathds R^d is said to be a Feller process if its transition semigroup is a strongly continuous semigroup in the Banach space of continuous functions that vanish at infinity equipped with the uniform norm. A Markov process is said to have the strong Feller property if its transition semigroup maps bounded measurable functions to bounded continuous functions.

\begin{remark}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] According to Theorem \ref{t1-2} above, when $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant function and $\kappa(x,z)$
depends on $z$,
we can construct heat kernel associated with the operator $\LL$ when
$({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<\beta_0^{**}/{\alpha_2}$, which indicates that
the oscillation of the index function $\alpha(x)$ could not be too large.
We note that in \cite{BK2}, the elliptic Harnack inequality for $\LL$ was established under similar assumptions on the index function $\alpha(x)$.
Note that by \eqref{t1-1-9a} and \eqref{t1-1-4b}, when $\alpha(x)\equiv \alpha \in (0,2)$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$, two-sided estimates of heat kernel in Theorem \ref{t1-2} are reduced
to those in \cite{CZ}.

\item[(2)] As mentioned in Remark \ref{remark1}(2), Theorem \ref{t1-2} indeed provides us some sufficient conditions
for the existence of a strong Markov process (in fact a Feller process having the strong Feller property)
associated with $\LL$
when $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$. Note that, the existence of such
strong Markov process is required and assumed a prior in the proofs of
the H\"{o}lder continuity of harmonic functions in \cite{BK1} and
the elliptic Harnack inequality for $\LL$ in \cite{BK2}.

 \end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

We conclude this part with the following remarks on some possible extensions of Theorems \ref{t1-1} and \ref{t1-2}.


\begin{remark}\label{rrr-000}
\begin{itemize}
 \item[(1)] By carefully checking the arguments of Theorem \ref{t1-1}, one can see that Theorem \ref{t1-1} still holds true if the condition that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$ is replaced  by the following two assumptions on $\kappa(x,z)$:
\begin{itemize}
\item [(i)] For every fixed $x \in \mathds R^d$, $\kappa(x,\cdot):\mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+$
is a radial function, i.e., $\kappa(x,z)$ only depends on $|z|$.

\item [(ii)] Let $j(x,r)=\wt \kappa(x,r)r^{-d-\alpha(x)}$ for $x \in \mathds R^d$ and $r>0$, where
$\wt \kappa(x,r):=\kappa(x,z)$ with $|z|=r$. For every $x \in \mathds R^d$, $j(x,\cdot)$ is non-increasing and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ such that the function $r\mapsto -\frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial j(x,r)}{\partial r}$ is non-increasing.
\end{itemize}

\item[(2)] Let $\wt \LL f(x)=\LL f(x)+\langle b(x), \nabla f(x)\rangle$, where $b:\mathds R^d\rightarrow \mathds R^d$ is bounded and uniformly
H\"older continuous.
It is possible to extend Theorems \ref{t1-1} and \ref{t1-2}  to $\wt \LL$ under the assumption that $\alpha_1>1$,
When $\alpha_1>1$, the gradient perturbation $\langle b(x), \nabla \rangle$ is of lower order than $\LL$.
We  refer the readers to
\cite{BJ, CD, CH, JS, MM, MM1,XZ}
on heat kernel estimates associated
with non-local operators under gradient perturbation.
For heat kernel estimates associated
with non-local operators under non-local perturbations, see \cite{CW, W, CHXZ}.


\item[(3)] By combining with the approach from \cite{CZ4},
it is possible to remove the symmetry assumption of $\kappa (x, z)$ in $z$.
But we will not pursue this extension  in this paper.

\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d} p^z(t-s,x-
z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\preceq
